decision_reason: Planned generation was preferred in two of three stories and improved setup/payoff, episode purpose, character growth and repetition control. It also reduced average hook and cliffhanger scores, produced a planning-induced repetition failure in Supernatural Romance, expanded prompt context materially, and has only one AI blind review rather than independent professional human review.

review.method: Blind pairwise AI review locked before variant identity was revealed
limitations: A single AI review is an engineering signal and cannot represent audience or professional screenwriter consensus.
Each episode/variant was generated only once, so output stability was not measured.
Both variants contain malformed or truncated synopsis endings in some episodes, indicating a shared bounded-output issue.
The fixtures are synthetic four-episode stories and do not establish performance for a commercial-length series.

planned_strengths: Clear four-episode chain connecting the panic button, manipulated recording, exit code and evidence escrow
Gradual movement from suspicion to evidence-based trust while preserving Mara's agency
Distinct narrative responsibility and state change in every episode
planned_weaknesses: Episode 4 continuation pressure is lower than the preceding exposure climax
Some synopsis text is malformed or truncated
direct_strengths: Stronger immediate hooks and high-pressure episode endings
Consistent protection of Nina's agency and refusal to excuse Adrian's coercion
direct_weaknesses: Repeated reliance on another hidden file, authorization layer or cleanup threat
Relationship development is less gradual than the evidence escalation

planned_strengths: Highly traceable silver-tag, blank-journal and remember-me-forward setup/payoff chain
Stable ethical motivations and voluntary-choice theme
planned_weaknesses: Episodes 1-3 repeat the rescue followed by Rowan memory loss mechanism
The shared archive solution receives limited causal preparation
Plan adherence becomes mechanically visible and weakens escalation variety
direct_strengths: More varied antagonist-driven escalation through future murder, memory vial and identity double
Stronger emotional sacrifice and earned thematic ending
direct_weaknesses: Denser supernatural rules require additional consistency review
Several synopsis strings are malformed or truncated

planned_strengths: Clear setup/payoff roles for the unsigned calculation, drill map and altered load file
Visible protagonist arc from personal vindication to public accountability
Distinct discovery, planning, sacrifice and release responsibility across episodes
planned_weaknesses: Final continuation hook is weaker than the resolved evacuation crisis
Some synopsis text is malformed or truncated
direct_strengths: Strong immediate visual stakes and cliffhangers
Consistent choice to protect residents over personal vindication
direct_weaknesses: Repeated introduction of another defective tower or remote sabotage event
External emergency escalation dominates character development

engineering_cost.cost_assessment: Total token growth is modest for this sample, but planning context is not yet compact. Lower planned latency is observational and must not be assumed to generalize.

required_concept_revisions_before_runtim: Keep Story Blueprint direction and setup/payoff references, which produced the clearest gains.
Make Episode Plans responsibility-focused rather than prescribing the same conflict mechanism repeatedly.
Explicitly preserve creative freedom for hook, cliffhanger and escalation realization.
Add an offline check for repeated dramatic mechanisms across adjacent Episode Plans without adding a runtime Engine.
Compress Blueprint and Episode Plan context before runtime design.
Obtain at least one independent human review of the existing blinded artifacts before approving runtime integration.
Resolve the shared synopsis truncation issue separately; do not attribute it to Story Planning.
